# Balance projection

**Generated by `node tools/regenerate-projection.js`. Do not hand-edit.**

Simulated against Cory's actual training week: Upper/Lower twice weekly at real working
weights, three runs, daily steps, sleep, water, reading, meditation. Consistency modelled
at 75%, which is honest rather than optimistic. The simulation is seeded, so this table
is reproducible: `src/domain/balance-projection.js` runs the real XP engine against the
real `data/balance.json`.

| Day | Might | Wind | Grit | Vitality | Mind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 60 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 3 |
| 90 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| 180 | 7 | 5 | 6 | 6 | 5 |
| 365 | 9 | 7 | 8 | 8 | 7 |

Year-end rank **B**, 39 total attribute levels.

## Checks

- Every attribute reaches level 3 by day 60 — **pass**
- Nothing reaches the level 10 cap within a year — **pass**
- Spread at 365 is 2 levels — **pass** (target <= 3)

## What the retune changed

The values this project shipped with were a considered first guess that had never been
run. Simulated, they collapsed: Might reached the cap by day 60 and every other attribute
by day 180, finishing the year at rank S with all five maxed. A year of training had
nothing left to give after two months.

Two things were wrong, and only one of them was a rate.

**The curve was far too shallow.** `base` 260 with exponent 1.85 puts level 10 at
roughly 18,000 XP — about three weeks of lifting. The two anchors in `docs/01` pin the
curve down completely: level 1 must fall inside the first session, and level 10 near a
year. That ratio is roughly the number of sessions in a year, so the exponent has to be
near 2.45, not 1.85. `base` is now 400, which is one honest first session.

**Might outscored everything else five to one.** Volume XP scales with load moved, and
load moved is a big number. Might's rates came down to roughly a third; the other four
moved by less than 35% in either direction. Might still leads, which is correct for a
training app, but by two levels rather than by a cap.

**Bodyweight movements now carry load.** Each has a fixed `notionalLoad` in
`data/exercises.json` — pull-up 120, dip 100, hanging leg raise 60, single-leg calf
raise 40 — credited per rep, with any added weight stacked on top. The plank is scored by
time, not load, so it has none. The constant belongs to the exercise and not to the
person: it is never the user's body weight and never derived from it, which is what keeps
a heavier lifter from earning more Might than a lighter one. This lifted Might slightly in
the early weeks without moving the year-end profile.

## For Claude Code

The checks above are enforced by `src/domain/balance.projection.test.js`, which also
compares this table against a fresh simulation. Changing `data/balance.json` without
regenerating this file fails the suite.

These numbers are a considered starting point, not scripture. Retune freely — but
regenerate this table whenever you do.
